text: Sixty-six million years ago, in a valley of giant ferns, a young Triceratops named Kira was born last of her herd. She was smaller than the others. Slower. Her horns were barely bumps. The elders said she would never survive a single dry season. [pause] But Kira had something the others didn't. She noticed things. The birds going quiet. The water in the river turning warm. The ground humming beneath her feet.

[pause] One night, she couldn't sleep. The stars were hidden behind a red glow. She nudged her mother, but her mother only grunted and rolled over. [pause] Then the mountain woke up. [excited] A roar louder than any predator split the sky. Fire burst from the peak. Burning rocks rained down on the valley. The herd panicked and stampeded into the dark. And in all that chaos, nobody noticed that the smallest Triceratops had been left behind.

When morning came, the valley was gone. Grey ash covered everything like snow. Kira called out for her mother again and again. [pause] Only silence answered. She followed the deep footprints of the herd, but the wind was already burying them. Her stomach ached. Her legs shook. [pause] Then she heard it. A low, rumbling breath behind the broken trees. Something huge was moving.

Something that had smelled her. [whispering] Kira froze. [pause] From the smoke stepped a Tyrannosaurus. One eye was clouded white. A long scar ran down his jaw. Every creature in the valley knew his name. Old Scar. [pause] He lowered his head and sniffed the air. Kira's heart pounded so hard she was sure he could hear it. Then he opened his jaws, and Kira did the only thing she could. She ran.

Kira crashed through the ferns, Old Scar's footsteps shaking the earth behind her. Branches whipped her face. The ground ended at a cliff. [pause] Below was a river of black, cooling lava. Behind her, the giant was getting closer. [pause] Then a shadow passed over her. A Pteranodon swooped down, screeching, and slammed its wings into Old Scar's good eye.

The tyrant roared and stumbled backwards into the smoke. [pause] The flying reptile landed on a rock beside Kira. She was scruffy, with a torn wing and sharp, curious eyes. [chuckling] Kira later named her Zephyr. [pause] Zephyr tilted her head, as if to say, you are very bad at surviving. Kira snorted. But when Zephyr took off toward the north, toward the green hills where the herd might be, Kira followed. For the first time since the fire, she was not alone.

For three days they travelled north. Zephyr scouted from the sky. Kira found water by listening to the ground. [pause] On the fourth day they reached a valley full of bones. Huge white ribs rose from the dust like the walls of a ruined city. Nothing grew there. Nothing moved. [whispering] Zephyr refused to land. [pause] In the middle of the bones, Kira found a nest.

Inside were broken shells, and one egg that was still warm. She pressed her face against it. Something tapped back from inside. [pause] Then the ground trembled. Not from the mountain this time. From footsteps. [sad] Old Scar had followed them the entire way. He was limping, starving, and angrier than ever. Kira looked at the egg. She could run, like she always did. Or she could stay. [long pause] Kira lowered her tiny horns and planted her feet.

Old Scar charged. The bones shook. Kira did not move. [pause] At the last second she dodged sideways, and the giant crashed headfirst into a wall of ancient ribs. The bones collapsed on top of him in a cloud of dust. [pause] He rose again, roaring. But before he could strike, Zephyr dropped from the sky, shrieking, clawing at his face.

Kira charged and slammed her horns into his leg with every bit of strength she had. [excited] Old Scar fell. [pause] For a long moment, nothing moved. Then the tyrant slowly got up, looked at the tiny Triceratops, and did something no one had ever seen him do. [pause] He walked away. [pause] Behind Kira, the egg cracked. A little head pushed through the shell. A baby Triceratops blinked up at her and squeaked. Kira wasn't the smallest anymore.

Kira, Zephyr, and the hatchling crossed the last hill together. And there, in a valley full of fresh green ferns, stood the herd. [pause] Her mother saw her first. She ran faster than Kira had ever seen her run, and pressed her great head against her daughter's. The elders stared at the little Triceratops who had crossed the burning lands, faced Old Scar, and brought back a new life.

[pause] Nobody called her too small again. [pause] That night, the herd slept peacefully for the first time in weeks. But Kira couldn't sleep. She noticed things, remember? [pause] And high above the valley, a new light was burning in the sky. Brighter than any star. Growing bigger every night. [whispering] Zephyr looked up and went very, very quiet. [long pause] Some stories end. And some stories are only the beginning.
